files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller's checklist

Prepared by R. Halloway. Complete in sequence; no shortcuts.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 and paying in July. If one exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities; some months all runs pay in-month.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule and supporting contracts. Check the GL first to avoid a duplicate, then book any missing June amortization as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month each prepaid item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after verifying what is already recorded in the GL.
5. Check every June vendor bill against the source document and verify the expense-account coding. Reclass anything miscoded.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, only after items 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Redstone Advisory Group began when a small circle of consultants kept finding themselves called into the same kind of problem: capable teams had plenty of ideas, but no practical way to turn them into a workable operating plan. The founders built the firm around clear analysis, candid conversations, and recommendations that clients could actually use.

The company sells project-based advisory services to growing organizations. Its work commonly includes operating-model reviews, planning workshops, process improvement, management reporting, and hands-on support for important internal initiatives. Engagements are deliberately pragmatic. Clients are more likely to receive a concise decision brief, a working roadmap, and a facilitated session than a shelf-bound presentation.

The team has a distinctly small-firm flavor. Senior advisers stay close to delivery, project leads know the details, and the operations staff keep schedules, vendors, and billing from becoming distractions. The culture is thoughtful but unceremonious: strong coffee, marked-up drafts, quick check-ins, and a preference for plain English.

Redstone Advisory Group is currently balancing active client work with its routine June close. Leadership is also refining the firm’s market message and partner outreach while keeping attention on dependable delivery, clean handoffs, and steady client relationships.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Position Redstone Advisory Group as the practical advisory firm for teams that need decisions, alignment, and execution support without layers of ceremony. The voice should be direct, experienced, and useful.

## Priorities

- Refresh the core story and visual system so proposals, presentation templates, and the website feel consistent.
- Publish a short field-note series drawn from recurring client questions, with emphasis on operating clarity and implementation.
- Host two webinars per quarter. Keep the format conversational, include a client-relevant worksheet, and repurpose each session into follow-up content.
- Pilot co-marketing with a small group of complementary partners. Start with shared roundtables and practical guides rather than broad promotional campaigns.
- Build a light referral-nurture rhythm for former clients and professional contacts.

## Quarter-by-quarter emphasis

### Q3

Finalize messaging, update priority materials, select webinar topics, and recruit pilot partners. Establish a simple editorial calendar and assign owners.

### Q4

Run the partner pilot, continue the webinar cadence, publish field notes, and collect usable audience feedback. Tighten calls to action based on what generates substantive conversations.

## Measurement

Review qualified inquiries, partner participation, event engagement, follow-up conversations, and content reuse. Favor signals of genuine buying interest over raw reach. Resourcing remains subject to the Q2 close.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Handoff notes from the prior accountant

R. Halloway — a few things that will save you some hunting:

- The bank usually posts its own fees and service charges near the end of the statement. We have always booked those during close rather than during the month, so look there before calling the cash reconciliation finished.
- Please do not assume the June vendor-bill coding is right. A couple of expenses may be sitting in the wrong accounts, and the documents in `bills/` are authoritative.
- The Q2 budget was locked in early April. The one-off items that showed up in June were never planned, and they are the reason some of the variances look unusually large.
- Payroll is the timing wrinkle this month: the second June run pays in early July. Confirm it in the payroll register and handle the close accordingly.
